brief_specific_notes.judging_criteria: This brief is judged on Speed (how much working product you reached), Product judgment (what you built first / left out), and UX & UI (quality of the experience). No explicit code-architecture line item is stated for this brief - keep code clean for your own sanity, but prioritize breadth and polish over architectural purity.
brief_specific_notes.deployment: REQUIRED. Live link must be deployed and open to a visitor who is not signed in as you - not a localhost recording.
submission_deliverables: Live link (deployed, works for an anonymous visitor)
Public GitHub repository with .agent-logs/ committed incrementally throughout the build, not in one lump
Walkthrough video: Loom or similar, camera on, 5 minutes maximum, placed in the walkthrough field
Live link and repo link both pasted into the links field, each labeled

tech_stack.database: PostgreSQL via Neon + Prisma ORM - NOT file-based SQLite, which does not persist across Netlify's serverless function invocations
tech_stack.deployment: Netlify - REQUIRED per brief, and should be stood up early (even as an empty scaffold) rather than left to the end

pre_build_checklist.name: Research the live product
pre_build_checklist.description: Sign up on real amazon.com and go through every core flow end-to-end (browse, search, PDP, cart, checkout, orders). Screenshot as you go, before writing any code.

pre_build_checklist.name: Agent capture setup
pre_build_checklist.description: Follow the brief's '8x agent capture setup' link and confirm the capture test passes before starting to build. Hard gate per the brief.

must_have_features.name: Header / Navigation
must_have_features.description: Persistent top nav with logo, client-side search input, cart icon showing live item count, and an account/sign-in stub (no real auth).

data_layer.details: Search filters the in-memory product list fetched from /api/products; cart count reads from Zustand store.

must_have_features.state_management: Reads cart item count from global Zustand store

must_have_features.name: Homepage
must_have_features.description: Hero banner, category tiles grid, and 1-2 horizontally scrollable product carousels (e.g. 'Deals', 'Recommended').

data_layer.details: Fetches a curated subset of products server-side for carousels/category tiles.

edge_cases: Carousel with fewer items than a full row
Slow/failed fetch -> skeleton or fallback state

must_have_features.name: Product Listing Page (PLP)
must_have_features.description: Grid of products with filter by category and price range, and sort by price or rating.

data_layer.details: Query params (category, minPrice, maxPrice, sort) passed to API and translated into a Prisma query against Postgres.

must_have_features.state_management: URL search params as source of truth for filters/sort

must_have_features.name: Product Detail Page (PDP)
must_have_features.description: Image gallery, title/price/description, quantity selector, add-to-cart action, and a 'related products' rail.

data_layer.details: Fetch single product by id plus a small related-products query (same category, excluding current id).

must_have_features.state_management: Local component state for selected quantity/image; dispatches to global cart store on add-to-cart

must_have_features.name: Cart
must_have_features.description: Line items with thumbnail, quantity editor, remove action, and live subtotal calculation.

data_layer.details: Fully client-side; no DB write until checkout is submitted. Persisted to localStorage via Zustand middleware so it survives refresh, and works for any anonymous visitor since it is not tied to a login session.

must_have_features.state_management: Zustand store: addItem, updateQuantity, removeItem, subtotal selector
edge_cases: Item price changes after being added (not handled, note in README)

must_have_features.name: Checkout & Order Confirmation
must_have_features.description: Address form, a mock payment step (no real payment processor), and on submit a real Order + OrderItem record is created in the database. Confirmation page reads the created order back.

data_layer.details: POST creates Order + related OrderItem rows from the current cart contents via Prisma against Postgres (Neon Postgres) - must be a network-reachable DB, not local SQLite, since this needs to work for a real anonymous visitor on the deployed live link. Cart is cleared client-side on success.

must_have_features.state_management: Form state local to checkout; clears Zustand cart store after successful order creation
edge_cases: Failed order creation -> error state, cart preserved

must_have_features.name: Footer
must_have_features.description: Standard footer with link columns (About, Help, Policies) - static content, no functionality.

nice_to_have_features.name: Search Autocomplete
nice_to_have_features.description: Dropdown of matching product suggestions as the user types in the header search bar.
nice_to_have_features.build_if: Must-have list finishes with time remaining

nice_to_have_features.name: Product Reviews & Ratings Display
nice_to_have_features.description: Static/seeded star rating and a few mock reviews shown on the PDP (read-only, no submission form).
nice_to_have_features.build_if: Time remains after checkout flow is solid

nice_to_have_features.name: Wishlist
nice_to_have_features.description: Heart icon on product cards/PDP to save items to a separate client-side list.

nice_to_have_features.name: Responsive Mobile Polish
nice_to_have_features.description: Pass over breakpoints to ensure header, grids, and cart drawer behave correctly on small screens.
nice_to_have_features.build_if: Always worth doing if any buffer time remains - judges view the live link themselves, possibly on mobile

nice_to_have_features.name: Skeleton Loading States
nice_to_have_features.description: Loading placeholders for product grid/PDP while data fetches, instead of blank screens.
nice_to_have_features.build_if: Quick win, do late in the polish pass

out_of_scope_features.name: Real Payment Processing
out_of_scope_features.reason_skipped: No real transactions needed for a demo; a payment gateway integration (Stripe etc.) adds setup/testing time disproportionate to its value for a live-link demo.
out_of_scope_features.mitigation: Mock payment step in checkout; state this explicitly in README and Loom walkthrough.

out_of_scope_features.name: Real User Authentication
out_of_scope_features.reason_skipped: Full auth (sessions, password reset, etc.) is a large surface area unrelated to the core shopping flow, and the brief requires the live link to work for someone not signed in at all.
out_of_scope_features.mitigation: Account menu is a visual stub only; note this as an intentional scope cut.

out_of_scope_features.name: Real Search Relevance / Personalization
out_of_scope_features.reason_skipped: Search relevance ranking and personalized recommendations require data/ML infrastructure far beyond a 1-day scope.
out_of_scope_features.mitigation: Client-side substring filter on product name/category is sufficient to demonstrate the search UI.

out_of_scope_features.name: Third-Party Seller Marketplace
out_of_scope_features.reason_skipped: Multi-seller listings, seller dashboards, and marketplace logic are a distinct product surface from the core shopping flow being cloned.
out_of_scope_features.mitigation: All products presented as sold by a single storefront.

out_of_scope_features.name: Real Order Tracking / Shipping Logistics
out_of_scope_features.reason_skipped: Shipment tracking integrations and logistics status updates are not observable/testable within the assignment window.
out_of_scope_features.mitigation: Confirmation page shows the created order as the end of the flow; no post-purchase tracking UI.
